title: The yearbook photo, again
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The corkboard. The yearbook photo, two years pinned. MOST LIKELY TO WIN A PULITZER. Wood looks at it the way he looks at the bus schedule. He turns twenty in two weeks. The strip doesn't say so; it draws the photo with the pin loose.

panels.composition: The corkboard. The yearbook photo: WOOD at seventeen, the caption as blocks but for one line legible. The pin loose.

image.prompt: close on a corkboard with a yearbook photograph of a thin boy pinned loosely, one caption line legible, black and white, no words
image.notes: Letter after: MOST LIKELY TO WIN A PULITZER — Arthur Finch.

panels.composition: Wood looking at it. Twenty in two weeks. Not said.

image.prompt: a young man looking at a yearbook photo on a corkboard, hands in his coat, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood pressing the pin in. Firm. Not moving the photo. Same place.

image.prompt: close on a thumb pressing a loose pin firmly back into a corkboard, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The corkboard: the photo, the letter, the roster, the postcards facing the wall, the schedule. Two years of a wall. BARNABY asleep under it. The strip counts the pins. Eleven. That number again.

image.prompt: a corkboard crowded with pinned papers above a small dog asleep beneath, eleven pins visible, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The pin pressed back. Eleven pins. Twenty in two weeks; not said.
